sections.html:
Pine Bluff is the seat of Jefferson County in southeast Arkansas, on the Arkansas River about 43 miles southeast of Little Rock. The city has lost residents for decades. It peaked at about 57,400 people in 1970 and is estimated at 38,213 in 2025. Jefferson County peaked at 90,718 in 1980 and is estimated at 62,987 in 2025.

The 2020 housing count was 19,197 units, with 16.2% of them vacant and 16,086 households. Set your price with that vacancy rate in mind. Some listings linger for months, and an empty inherited house keeps collecting tax bills.

The city has been building since the 1830s, so the stock runs from Victorian houses west of Main Street to newer homes on the edge of town. Each era brings different repair worries, and a cash buyer weighs them house by house.

Pine Bluff sits on flat river-delta ground, with the Arkansas River, Lake Pine Bluff and Bayou Bartholomew nearby. A levee system runs 380 miles from Pine Bluff to Venice, Louisiana, but buyers still ask about flooding, and the 1927 flood is well remembered locally. Look up the FEMA flood map for your exact address before you list, because the ground under one street can differ from the next.

With about 53.6 inches of rain a year, the usual trouble spots in an older house are the roof, drainage around the foundation and moisture in the crawl space. If you know about any of these, say so up front. If you would rather not fix them first, an as-is sale lets the buyer take that work on.

sections.h2: Which school district is your house in?
sections.html:
Pine Bluff, Watson Chapel and White Hall all serve parts of the city. Streets can straddle them, so check your address before telling a buyer which schools apply.

Dollarway School District merged into Pine Bluff on July 1, 2021, and Dollarway High School closed in 2023. If an old listing or a neighbor still refers to Dollarway, the address now belongs to the Pine Bluff district.

The Jefferson County Tax Collector collects property and real estate taxes, municipal liens and business personal property tax. The office is at 101 West Barraque in Pine Bluff, open Monday through Friday, 8:30 am to 5:00 pm. The phone number is 870-541-5313.

TaskWhenWhere
Pay real estate taxMarch 1 to October 15Tax Collector, 101 West Barraque
Schedule an assessment hearingBy the third Monday in AugustCounty Board of Equalization
Ask about back taxesAny time, before you listTax Collector, 870-541-5313

Have the parcel number handy when you phone, so the balance can be looked up quickly.

sections.h2: Reappraisal, appeals and the homestead credit
sections.html:
Property here is revalued on a 3, 4 or 5 year cycle set by the state. When a new value looks too high, you can ask for a hearing in front of the County Board of Equalization, and the request has to be on the calendar by the third Monday in August. Collect photos of damage, repair quotes and recent sales of similar houses before you go.

Owners who live in the house can claim a homestead credit worth up to $500 a year, and the cap moves to up to $600 beginning with 2026 tax bills. Amendment 79 also keeps a homestead's taxable value from climbing more than 5% in a year. If a buyer will live there, suggest they file for the credit once the deed is in their name.

Taxes that go unpaid can end in a sale run by the Commissioner of State Lands. In 2023 that office sold just over 200 Jefferson County properties, most of them for under $500. Owners who lose a house that way get no say in the price.

Owing back taxes does not block a sale. A workable order of steps:

  • Call the Tax Collector and ask for the full balance on the parcel.
  • Locate the deed and your newest tax bill.
  • Tell the buyer or title company about the balance early so it can be paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  • Ask that the closing statement show the payoff to the collector.

The sooner you act, the less interest and cost eat into your proceeds.

Pine Bluff is one of three Delta cities that worked with Community Progress for about 18 months on plans for vacant, abandoned and deteriorated properties. Jefferson County is among the 20 Arkansas counties with the highest residential vacancy rates.

  • The urban renewal agency and the code enforcement department hold "Green Sweeps" to teach owners about maintenance duties.
  • The urban renewal agency and public works host monthly free dump days for large household items.
  • An owner who lives elsewhere should mow, clear the yard and secure the building.

If a neighbor or inspector reports the property, open any notice the day it arrives and call the number listed on it.

Letters about overgrown lots or damaged buildings come from the city, not the county, so check which office sent a notice before you respond. An as-is cash sale removes the cleaning, repair and staging work from a vacant house, which is why it is common for inherited and out-of-town ownership here.

sections.h2: What a cash sale skips, and what to bring
sections.html:
Listing the usual way means cleanup, repairs, open houses and a wait on the buyer's loan approval. Selling for cash skips nearly all of it, a real advantage where empty houses are common. The buyer sees the property in its current condition, names a price, and closes when you both choose.

Pull these papers together first:

  • The deed, or for an inherited house, the court papers that show you can sign.
  • The most recent Jefferson County tax statement.
  • A payoff letter, if a mortgage or lien remains.
  • Notes on repairs you know the house needs, including roof leaks and moisture under the floor.

A buyer who sees them can quote a firmer number, and the title company can start its search right away.

Recording a deed in Arkansas means buying a transfer stamp at $3.30 for each $1,000 of consideration, and a further $2.20 per $1,000 is assigned to the purchaser. Decide in the contract who buys the stamp, and have the closing agent verify both figures.

Arkansas does not require every seller to complete a disclosure form, but listing agents must make reasonable efforts to learn material facts. Form or no form, be straight with a buyer about the roof, foundation and any water trouble.

faqs.q: How many people live in Pine Bluff?
faqs.a: Roughly 38,213 in 2025, down from 41,253 in 2020 and 49,083 in 2010.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Jefferson County property tax?
faqs.a: Go to the Tax Collector's office at 101 West Barraque, or phone 870-541-5313. The collection window opens March 1 and closes October 15.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Pine Bluff house in?
faqs.a: It depends on the address. The city is served by the Pine Bluff, Watson Chapel and White Hall districts, and Dollarway merged into Pine Bluff on July 1, 2021.

faqs.q: What happens to a Pine Bluff house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: It can be certified to the Commissioner of State Lands and sold at the annual sale. Properties that do not sell move to a post-auction list.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited Pine Bluff house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. Selling as-is for cash means no repairs or cleanout on your end. Start by locating the deed and the most recent tax bill.
